arxiv-1908-11538.title: IoT based Smart Access Controlled Secure Smart City Architecture Using Blockchain
arxiv-1908-11538.creator: Rourab Paul 1 , Nimisha Ghosh 2 , Suman Sau 2 Amlan Chakrabarti 3 , Prasant Mahapatra 4
arxiv-1908-11538.description: Abstract Standard security protocols like SSL, TLS, IPSec etc. have high memory and processor consumption which makes all these security protocols unsuitable for resource constrained platforms such as Internet of Things (IoT). Blockchain (BC) finds its efficient application in IoT platform to preserve the five basic cryptographic primitives, such as confidentiality, authenticity, integrity, availability and non-repudiation.

arxiv-2003-07884.title: Lipschitz stability for an inverse source problem in anisotropic parabolic equations with dynamic boundary conditions
arxiv-2003-07884.creator: E. M. Ait Ben Hassi, S. E. Chorfi, L. Maniar, O. Oukdach
arxiv-2003-07884.description: Abstract . In this paper, we study an inverse problem for linear parabolic system with variable diffusion coefficients subject to dynamic boundary conditions. We prove a global Lipschitz stability for the inverse problem involving a simultaneous recovery of two source terms from a single measurement and interior observations, based on a recent Carleman estimate for such problems.

arxiv-2005-05233.title: Fermi surface and kink structures in Sr 4 Ru 3 O 10 revealed by synchrotron-based ARPES
arxiv-2005-05233.creator: Prosper Ngabonziza, Emanuela Carleschi, Volodymyr Zabolotnyy, Amina Taleb-Ibrahimi, François Bertran, Rosalba Fittipaldi, Veronica Granata, Mario Cuoco, Antonio Vecchione, Bryan Patrick Doyle
arxiv-2005-05233.description: Abstract Abstract The low-energy electronic structure, including the Fermi surface topology, of the itinerant metamagnet Sr 4 Ru 3 O 10 is investigated for the first time by synchrotron-based angle-resolved photoemission. Well-defined quasiparticle band dispersions with matrix element dependencies on photon energy or photon polarization are presented.

arxiv-2201-06955.title: Understanding COVID-19 Effects on Mobility: A Community-Engaged Approach DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Journal: JACM Volume: 37 4 111 8 CCS: Information systems applications Data mining CCS: Decision support systems Data analytics
arxiv-2201-06955.creator: Arun Sharma, Majid Farhadloo, Yan Li, Aditya Kulkarni, Jayant Gupta, Shashi Shekhar
arxiv-2201-06955.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Arun Sharma, Majid Farhadloo, Yan Li, Aditya Kulkarni, Jayant Gupta, Shashi Shekhar. Given aggregated mobile device data, the goal is to understand the impact of COVID-19 policy interventions on mobility. This problem is vital due to important societal use cases, such as safely reopening the economy. Challenges include understanding and interpreting questions of interest to policymakers, cross-jurisdictional variability in choice and time of interventions, the large data volume, and unknown sampling bias.

arxiv-2203-00164.title: Quantum jumbled pattern matching
arxiv-2203-00164.creator: Julio Juárez-Xochitemol, Edgar Chávez
arxiv-2203-00164.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Julio Juárez-Xochitemol, Edgar Chávez. Let S 1 , S 2 ∈ Σ ∗ S_{1},S_{2}\in\Sigma^{*} strings, we say that S 1 S_{1} jumble match S 2 S_{2} if they are permutations of each other. Given a text T T of size N N and a string S ∈ Σ ∗ S\in\Sigma^{*} , the problem of Jumbled Pattern Matching (JPM) is to determine all substrings in T T jumbled matching S S .

arxiv-2206-04392.title: Binary parameters from astrometric and spectroscopic errors–candidate hierarchical triples and massive dark companions in Gaia DR3 2022 Binary parameters from astrometric and spectroscopic errors–candidate hierarchical triples and massive dark companions in Gaia DR3 – 23
arxiv-2206-04392.creator: Shion Andrew, Zephyr Penoyre, Vasily Belokurov, N. Wyn Evans, Semyeong Oh
arxiv-2206-04392.description: Abstract We show how astrometric and spectroscopic errors introduced by an unresolved binary system can be combined to give estimates of the binary period and mass ratio. This can be performed analytically if we assume we see one or more full orbits over our observational baseline, or numerically for all other cases.

arxiv-2405-14060.title: Probabilistic Inference in the Era of Tensor Networks and Differential Programming
arxiv-2405-14060.creator: Martin Roa-Villescas, Xuanzhao Gao, Sander Stuijk, Henk Corporaal, Jin-Guo Liu
arxiv-2405-14060.description: Abstract Probabilistic inference is a fundamental task in modern machine learning. Recent advances in tensor network (TN) contraction algorithms have enabled the development of better exact inference methods. However, many common inference tasks in probabilistic graphical models (PGMs) still lack corresponding TN-based adaptations.

arxiv-2501-18061.title: Experimenting with the Garsia–Milne Involution Principle This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Basic Hypergeometric Series Associated with Root Systems and Applications in honor of Stephen C. Milne’s 75th birthday. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA
arxiv-2501-18061.creator: Shalosh B. EKHAD and Doron ZEILBERGER
arxiv-2501-18061.description: Abstract In 1981, Adriano Garsia and Steve Milne found the first bijective proof of the celebrated Rogers–Ramanujan identities. To achieve this feat, they invented a versatile tool that they called the Involution Principle. In this note we revisit this useful principle from a very general perspective, independent of its application to specific combinatorial identities, and will explore its complexity.

arxiv-2506-00603.title: Modelling laminar flow in V-shaped filters integrated with catalyst technologies for atmospheric pollutant removal
arxiv-2506-00603.creator: Samuel D. Tomlinson, Aliki M. Tsopelakou, Tzia Ming Onn, Steven R. H. Barrett, Adam M. Boies, Shaun Fitzgerald
arxiv-2506-00603.description: Abstract Atmospheric pollution from particulate matter, volatile organic compounds and greenhouse gases is a critical environmental and public health issue, leading to respiratory diseases and climate change. A potential mitigation strategy involves utilising ventilation systems, which process large volumes of indoor and outdoor air and remove particulate pollutants through filtration.

pmc-10505015.creator: Michaela E Dungan, Mitchell Scheiman, Chang Yaramothu
pmc-10505015.description: PurposeTo develop a novel Vision Quality of Life (QoL) survey that emphasizes the amount of time a visual activity can be performed before symptoms occur.MethodsThe Vision Quality of Life with Time (VisQuaL-T) survey was developed with 10 daily activities and a list of common visual symptoms. Participants were recruited from a university campus.

pmc-11635438.title: Shipment of Cyanobacteria by Agarose Gel Embedding (SCAGE)—A Novel Method for Simple and Robust Delivery of Cyanobacteria
pmc-11635438.creator: Phillipp Fink, Jong-Hee Kwon, Karl Forchhammer
pmc-11635438.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In modern science, the exchange of scientific material between different institutions and collaborating working groups constitutes an indispensable endeavor. For this purpose, bacterial strains are frequently shipped to collaborators to advance joint research projects. Bacterial strains are usually safely shipped as cultures on solid medium, whereas the shipment of liquid cultures requires specific safety measures due to the risk of leakage. Cyanobacterial cultures are frequently maintained as liquid stock cultures, and this problem typically arises.

pmc-11710645.title: A systematic review with meta‐analysis of the GABAergic system in transgenic rodent models of amyloidosis and tauopathy
pmc-11710645.creator: André Nunes Mensch, Giovanna Carello‐Collar, Vanessa G. Ramos, Bruna Bellaver, Pamela C.L. Ferreira, Pedro Rosa‐Neto, Tharick A. Pascoal, Marco Antônio de Bastiani, Eduardo R. Zimmer
pmc-11710645.description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease (AD) is characterized by the accumulation of amyloid‐β (Aβ) plaques and tau tangles in the brain, and neurotransmission dysfunctions. Indeed, our group recently demonstrated that the γ‐aminobutyric acid (GABA)ergic system is vulnerable to AD pathology in humans. However, whether this vulnerability is also present in AD rodent models is still unknown.

pmc-12473051.title: Real-Time PCR Test (Flora Select™) for Assessing the Effectiveness of Bacterial Vaginosis Treatment During Pregnancy
pmc-12473051.creator: Hajime Ota, Shigeki Shimada, Yuta Kobayashi, Tatsuya Yoshiwara, Osamu Yoshino, Yoshiyuki Fukushi, Shinichiro Wada, Soromon Kataoka, Hideto Yamada, Garth Ehrlich, Antonella d’Arminio Monforte, Jun-Hyung Cho
pmc-12473051.description: Preterm birth is a major cause of perinatal mortality and morbidity in newborns, and its risk is increased by bacterial vaginosis (BV) during pregnancy. This multicenter prospective cohort study aimed to evaluate whether Flora select™ (FS), a newly developed real-time polymerase chain reaction test, is clinically useful for assessing the effectiveness of BV treatment during pregnancy.

pmc-12511584.title: Self-control as a mediator between caregiver burden and psychological resilience among psychiatric caregivers in Oman
pmc-12511584.creator: Al Reem Al Marshoudi, Maram Al Aisaiee, Al Zahraa Al Ghafri, Abdullah Al Ghailani, Naser Al Balushi, Mohammed Al Alawi
pmc-12511584.description: Caregivers of individuals with chronic psychiatric disorders are frequently exposed to high subjective burden, which may undermine their psychological resilience. Trait Emotional Intelligence (TEI), particularly its self-control facet, has been proposed as a protective factor; however, the mechanisms linking caregiver burden, self-control, and resilience are not well established.

pmc-12577614.title: Identification of Prognostic Gene Signatures for Survival of Patients With Phaeochromocytoma, Paraganglioma, and Other Tumor Types
pmc-12577614.creator: EDNAH OOKO, THOMAS EFFERTH
pmc-12577614.description: Background/AimTumor treatments remain unsatisfactory, as many patients continue to die despite therapy. There is an urgent need for novel drug targets, particularly for rare tumors. In this study, we sought to identify genes with prognostic significance for survival in patients with phaeochromocytoma or paraganglioma. We also examined whether these genes are relevant in other tumor entities.

pmc-12988201.title: A deep learning framework for breast cancer diagnosis using Swin Transformer and Dual-Attention Multi-scale Fusion Network
pmc-12988201.creator: Murdhy A. Aldawsari, Saad Jamhan Aldosari, Atef Ismail, Marwa M. Emam
pmc-12988201.description: Breast cancer is among the most prevalent cancers affecting women worldwide, and early detection through mammography is critical to reducing mortality rates. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated notable effectiveness in classifying mammograms. However, they are constrained in their ability to capture long-range contextual dependencies.

pmc-13448218.title: Multiparticle entanglement of nuclear spins in silicon
pmc-13448218.creator: Feng Xu, Yi Deng, Guangchong Hu, Kada Yang, Chunhui Li, Chao Wei, Shihang Zhang, Chunhui Zhang, Peng Du, Keji Shi, Mingchao Duan, Tianluo Pan, Zhen Tian, Peihao Huang, Guanyong Wang, Song Liu, Dapeng Yu, Yu He, Tao Xin
pmc-13448218.description: Silicon spin qubits offer high-fidelity control and semiconductor manufacturing compatibility. However, the systematic generation and characterization of multiparticle entanglement, a core resource for quantum information science, remain elusive in such systems. Here, we demonstrate the complete preparation of all nine canonical families of four-qubit entanglement between donor spins in silicon, by designing hardware-efficient quantum circuits that use native multi-qubit operations.
